primary.title: On the Origin of Species
primary.author: Charles Darwin
primary.rationale: Darwin's seminal work that introduced the theory of evolution by natural selection. It is a foundational text in biology and widely available.

primary.title: The Descent of Man, and Selection in Relation to Sex
primary.author: Charles Darwin
primary.rationale: This work applies Darwin's theory of natural selection to human evolution and sexual selection, offering further insights into his thought process.

primary.title: The Voyage of the Beagle
primary.author: Charles Darwin
primary.rationale: Darwin's journal of his travels on HMS Beagle, detailing his observations of geology and natural history that contributed to his later theories.

secondary.title: Darwin's Dangerous Idea: Evolution and the Meanings of Life
secondary.author: Daniel C. Dennett
secondary.rationale: A philosophical exploration of Darwin's ideas and their profound implications for our understanding of life and meaning, by a prominent philosopher.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Darwin
secondary.author: David L. Hull and Michael Ruse
secondary.rationale: A collection of essays by leading scholars covering various aspects of Darwin's life, work, and legacy, providing a comprehensive scholarly overview.

secondary.title: Charles Darwin: A Very Short Introduction
secondary.author: Jonathan R. S. Jones
secondary.rationale: A concise and accessible introduction to Darwin's life and scientific contributions, suitable for a broad academic audience.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources are foundational texts by Darwin. Secondary sources are scholarly analyses and companions published after 1976, offering critical perspectives on his work.
